idiom_name: two-constructor optional type (Some/None) with map/flatMap and a default at the call site
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one type with exactly two constructors - one carrying a present value, one marking absence - and make the constructors the only way to build it, so the empty state cannot be confused with a legitimate value. Provide one eliminator per consumer shape: matching/folding for the general case, map/flatMap so a chain of partial steps short-circuits at the first absence, and a defaulting exit (getOrElse/value_or/orElse) that names the policy at the call site. Convert at the boundary (from a nullable pointer, a missing key, a database column, an interop call) exactly once, and never let the empty state be represented as a sentinel of the payload type. Keep the reason for absence out of this type: when the caller must know why, move to a two-branch result type.
code_sketch:
type Maybe<T> = Just(T) | Nothing

find_user(id)    -> Maybe<User>
find_company(u)  -> Maybe<Company>

name = find_user(id)
    .and_then(find_company)      # short-circuits to Nothing
    .map(company_name)
    .get_or_else("unknown")      # default decided at the call site

match find_user(id):
    Just(u) -> use(u)
    Nothing -> handle_absent()    # both cases handled right here
pitfalls: Encoding absence as a sentinel value of the payload type defeats the constructors - the empty state must be a case of its own.
Adding the wrapper to every signature turns a code base into combinator chains; keep the classic structure where absence is real and let required values stay bare.
Where the type cannot nest (nullable references, C# string?), the Option<Option<T>> distinction must be modelled explicitly instead of being silently collapsed.

Wrong move: return Option/Maybe for a validation or I/O failure that callers must diagnose -> None erases the reason and makes recovery or observability impossible -> instead return Result/Either (or a domain-specific error) and reserve Option for ordinary absence.

Wrong move: unwrap, get, or force-unwrap immediately after every producer call -> the empty branch still crashes at runtime, only one frame later -> instead match/fold or compose map/flatMap, and use getOrElse or a proved-invariant throw only at the outer exit.

Wrong move: use Optional/Option as a parameter or field for every nullable property -> callers pay wrapping and the model gains two absence channels with serialization and interop friction -> instead keep required fields and parameters plain, model domain states explicitly, and use Option primarily for result boundaries.
